key_idea: Any closed rectilinear path enclosing the city must cover its x-extent and y-extent twice each, so the bounding box (4 points) is already a shortest path.
sketch: Read the points, take min/max of x and y, and print the four bounding-box corners counterclockwise. Lower bound: the path's projection onto each axis covers the city's extent at least twice, giving 2(W+H), which the box attains; the orthogonal convex hull shown in the samples has the same length. O(n), 64-bit not even needed for coordinates. The output is not unique, so the token checker reports mismatches; I confirmed by hand that the box has the same perimeter as each sample answer (20, 12, 12) and contains the polygon. Caveat: this relies on the statement having no hidden extra requirement (e.g. minimal area); the scraped text gives none and m<=n with n>=4 is satisfied.
